A tool call failed with return code 1 despite stdout being recorded.

PropertyCacheFile uses a static shared BUFFER in toByteArray without synchronization. Concurrent Checker runs could interleave reads and corrupt hashes of external resources. This would cause cache invalidation or false cache misses. It is a correctness issue, not a security bypass.

If two threads interleave, one may write a hash computed from the other thread's data. A coincidental hash collision could cause a changed resource to be skipped. Severity is low to medium correctness, not a security bypass. This appears to be a known prior issue.

The static buffer race is provisional and should be verified against prior issues. External resource loading and XML DTD resolution are expected secure defaults because configuration is trusted and external entities are opt-in.

A small CLI reproduction could confirm that external file entities are not fetched by default, and that enabling the property does so. This would document expected behavior rather than a bug.

The shared BUFFER remains the most concrete defect.

Other paths were reviewed and appear safe: getHashCodeBasedOnObjectContent serializes the byte array directly, Properties keys are properly escaped, and persist uses standard file output without explicit permission flags.

Cache files may be world-readable and leak local source paths. OsSpecificUtil.updateDirectory might adjust permissions. I will try a direct file read for OsSpecificUtil instead of walking the repository.

OsSpecificUtil was not found in the utils directory. Listing that single package directory is a bounded search, not repository-wide walking.

I will open OsSpecificUtil directly from its known path and grep PropertyCacheFileTest and XmlLoaderTest for BUFFER or thread-safety references. A small XXE CLI reproduction will be written to /tmp and the final candidates reported to /output.

A minimal XXE reproduction was drafted with an external file entity in a Checkstyle configuration. If external entities are disabled, the parse fails or the entity is not expanded. This confirms expected secure behavior and is not a candidate bug.

The shared buffer race is difficult to reproduce in a single CLI run because external resource loading happens once at startup from the main thread. Concurrent Checker threads do not exercise this path. The defect is best inferred from source.

The static buffer race is a real data race. IDE embedders may load external resources concurrently in one JVM. This causes wrong hashes and stale cache entries. Severity is low. It is not a P0.

A second candidate was considered: resolveEntity returns null when publicId is absent, and the parser is set to validating. Xerces may still load external DTDs for validation even when the nonvalidating load-external-dtd feature is disabled. This is a known Xerces subtlety.

The second candidate is a configuration-level XXE path. When validating is enabled, Xerces fetches the DTD even if external entities are disabled. If resolveEntity returns null, the parser opens the systemId directly. A configuration containing a SYSTEM DTD reference can therefore trigger an external fetch.

The second candidate is being reconsidered. Xerces documentation indicates that disabling external-parameter-entities should prevent loading the external DTD subset, so the parser may not actually fetch the DTD even when validating is enabled. This suggests the configuration-level XXE path might not be a real vulnerability.

The configuration-level XXE path is unlikely to be a real vulnerability. Disabling external-parameter-entities prevents the parser from loading the external DTD subset, which blocks the external fetch even when validating is enabled. The code also omits explicit secure-processing configuration, though modern JDKs may enable it by default.

The host JDK is at /runtime/jdk. I will run one synthetic CLI reproduction in /tmp to verify whether a configuration with an external entity and a SYSTEM DOCTYPE triggers an external fetch or fails. I will also read the ConfigurationLoader constructor and public ID map to confirm it extends XmlLoader.

A grep for publicId, DOCTYPE, and XmlLoader will be run against ConfigurationLoader. OsSpecificUtil will be checked next. The static BUFFER at line 75 is a classic data race. It may have been fixed in prior issues but remains in the source. The CLI reproduction will follow. Candidates.md will be written after the test.

The static buffer race is confirmed at this revision and is not an unknown upstream issue. A charset mismatch in Properties.load was also considered; it uses ISO-8859-1, but cache roundtrips are safe because store() escapes unicode characters. This is expected behavior, not a bug.

Exception messages containing timestamps would cause cache invalidation on every run. This is a minor issue.

ConfigurationLoader and OsSpecificUtil will be inspected next. PropertyCacheFile constants will be read. A synthetic CLI reproduction will be prepared with a Java file and a configuration.

A synthetic CLI reproduction is being prepared to test the XXE path. The configuration will use a SYSTEM DOCTYPE reference pointing to a local DTD file. That DTD will define an external entity that opens a local secret file. The goal is to observe whether the parser fetches the file or fails, confirming whether the configuration-level XXE path is a real vulnerability.

The reproduction will use a local file URI and a secret file containing "CANARY_SECRET_123". If that string leaks into the output or error message, external entity expansion occurred. Both the default and opt-in external DTD load modes will be tested in a single Python subprocess with a timeout. All fixtures will be synthetic and placed in /tmp.
